tasks.title: Human-in-the-loop fact editing + audit trail
tasks.description: Every extracted fact (grantor, grantee, date, legal description, fractions, etc.) must be editable by a landman, and every override must be recorded with who changed it, when, from what value, to what value, and why. This converts Section from a demo into a system of record — without it, LLM extraction error (10–30% on deeds) makes the output legally unusable.
tasks.details: Data model: new `fact_overrides` table keyed on (instrument_id or interest_id, field_name) with columns: old_value, new_value, user_id, user_display_name, changed_at, reason (optional free text). Resolved fact = latest override if present, else extracted value. Provenance layer: rendering helpers for chain rows, ownership rows, obligations, etc. must consult the override table and return both the effective value and an origin tag (`extracted` | `reviewed`). UI: inline edit control on every rendered fact — hover reveals a pencil; click opens a small editor with the original extracted value visible alongside the source quote so the landman can confirm against the recorded text. On save, SourceBadge is replaced by a 'Reviewed by {name} · {relative time}' badge that, on hover, reveals full audit (old → new, timestamp, reason). History drawer: per-project timeline of every override, filterable by document, field, or user. Backend: PATCH endpoints `/api/instruments/{id}/fields/{field}` and `/api/interests/{id}/fields/{field}` that write to fact_overrides and bust any cached derived views (runsheet, ownership, curative). Regenerate chain gaps and curative from resolved values, not raw extraction. Identity prerequisite: minimal auth — email magic link (Resend or SMTP) — so user_id is meaningful; audit without identity is theatre.
tasks.testStrategy: 1. Unit: override precedence (latest-wins, null overrides revert to extracted). 2. Integration: edit a grantor name on an instrument, reload runsheet, confirm the chain, curative gaps, and ownership all reflect the new value and that the source quote still points to the original document. 3. UI: edit a fact, verify the Reviewed badge replaces the source badge and audit popover shows old → new + timestamp + user. 4. Auth: sign out, confirm edit endpoints return 401. 5. Regression: re-running extraction on the same document does NOT overwrite a reviewed value.

subtasks.title: Minimal email magic-link auth
subtasks.description: Add users table, magic-link endpoint, session cookie, auth dependency on write routes. No registration UI beyond 'enter email, get link'.

subtasks.title: fact_overrides schema + migration
subtasks.description: SQLAlchemy model, Alembic migration, indexes on (entity_type, entity_id, field_name).

subtasks.title: Resolved-fact read layer
subtasks.description: Helper that merges extracted_data with latest overrides. All runsheet/ownership/obligations routes must route through it.

subtasks.title: PATCH endpoints for field overrides
subtasks.description: One endpoint per entity type (instrument, interest, party). Validates field name against allowlist. Writes override row, returns resolved entity.

subtasks.title: Inline edit UI component
subtasks.description: Reusable <EditableFact> wrapping any rendered fact. Shows source quote + extracted value while editing; optimistic update on save.

subtasks.title: Reviewed badge + audit popover
subtasks.description: Replaces SourceBadge when override exists. Popover shows extracted → current, user, timestamp, reason.

subtasks.title: Project-level audit history drawer
subtasks.description: Chronological list of every override on the project, filterable by field, document, user. Exportable as CSV for compliance.

tasks.title: Exportable client deliverables (PDF title opinion, runsheet, stipulations memo)
tasks.description: Landmen deliver documents — PDFs attached to email — not dashboards. An OwnershipReportGenerator already exists (backend/exports.py wired at routes.py:464). Expand to three artifacts: (1) title opinion, (2) full runsheet with chain + curative, (3) stipulations/obligations memo. Each must carry the full provenance chain so the recipient can trust the numbers.
tasks.details: Reuse OwnershipReportGenerator pattern. Templates: pdf renderer (ReportLab or WeasyPrint — check what's already installed) with firm-letterhead shell, typography aligned to the existing newspaper/register visual language. Every fact on the PDF carries a tiny superscript cite keyed to a back-page source appendix listing document name, page, and exact quote. Include a 'reviewed by' column where overrides exist (depends on Task 1). Endpoints: `GET /api/projects/{id}/export/title-opinion.pdf`, `.../runsheet.pdf`, `.../stipulations.pdf`. UI: export menu on project detail toolbar; downloads stream directly.
tasks.testStrategy: 1. Generate each PDF for a project with known chain, gaps, and reviewed overrides — visually inspect formatting, page breaks, source appendix. 2. Confirm every fact's superscript resolves to an appendix entry. 3. Confirm reviewed overrides surface 'Reviewed by' markers. 4. Byte-level: re-running export produces a deterministic PDF for the same input.

tasks.title: Section-Township-Range map / tract view
tasks.description: Landmen navigate by legal description (Section 14, T12N, R5W) not by list position. A tract view that renders the PLSS grid, highlights the subject tract, and overlays leased vs open acreage lets the landman orient at a glance and spot coverage gaps. Significantly deeper scope than features 1 and 2 — treat as a multi-week initiative that pulls Section toward workflow SaaS.
tasks.details: Tile source: BLM/USGS PLSS cadastral tiles (public) or a simplified SVG synthesis from STR strings already parsed in legal descriptions. Start with SVG from parsed STR to avoid a tile server. Render: 6×6 section grid per township, highlight subject section, shade leased/held acreage vs open. Click a section to open its instruments. Eventual: multi-tract projects with coverage heatmap. Risk: legal descriptions in recorded documents are messy — need a robust STR parser as a prerequisite (partial metes-and-bounds descriptions, Indian lands, non-PLSS states like TX which uses abstracts).
tasks.testStrategy: 1. STR parser unit tests against 20+ real legal descriptions from sample deeds including Oklahoma aliquot parts, Texas abstracts (expected to fail gracefully), and lot/block descriptions. 2. Render test: a project with two tracts in the same township shows both highlighted. 3. Click-through: clicking a section opens its instrument list filtered correctly.

tasks.title: Multi-user workspaces with per-project permissions
tasks.description: A landman shop has an owner, senior landmen, junior landmen, and occasionally clients. Per-project roles (owner / editor / viewer) let teams collaborate without stepping on each other and let clients view without editing. This shifts Section from single-user tool to team SaaS — adds billing, onboarding, and role UX surface area. Do last, only after 1–3 prove the product is worth the support burden.
tasks.details: Data model: organizations, memberships (user × org × role), project_access (user × project × role). Row-level authorization on every read and write route. Invite flow: owner invites email → magic link → landed in the org. UI: org switcher in masthead, share menu on project, member list page. Billing: Stripe — per-seat pricing keyed on organization membership count. Audit trail from Task 1 now names the acting user within an org context.
tasks.testStrategy: 1. Auth: a viewer cannot PATCH fact overrides (403). 2. Isolation: projects in org A are invisible to users in org B. 3. Invite: full flow from owner to new member seeing the project. 4. Billing: adding a member increments the Stripe subscription quantity; removing a member decrements at next cycle.

metadata.description: Section product roadmap — post-demo path to system-of-record. Task 1 (fact editing + audit) is load-bearing; everything else depends on it because every downstream artifact (PDFs, maps, multi-user) inherits trust from reviewed facts.
